quizzes.title: FIDE: Leadership and Recent Results
quizzes.passage:
FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs) is the International Chess Federation. It oversees major international competitions and sets the rules and rating standards that players follow. The federation is led by a President, with a Deputy President supporting its work.

Indian players have a long record in the sport. Viswanathan Anand is India's most successful chess player and has won the FIDE World Chess Championship in 2000, 2007, 2008, 2010 and 2012, a span of more than a decade. Koneru Humpy is India's highest-rated female chess player and has won the Women's World Rapid Chess Championship title.

In 2026, R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women's Candidates Tournament, and her win came in the final round of the event. She became the first Indian woman to claim its title. She will now challenge the reigning champion, Ju Wenjun, who currently holds the Women's World Chess Championship title, later in 2026.

Gukesh Dommaraju, India's youngest Grandmaster, became the youngest World Chess Champion after defeating Ding Liren in the FIDE World Chess Championship 2024. Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025, defeating Humpy Koneru in the final, and she became the third winner of that title after Alexandra Kosteniuk and Aleksandra Goryachkina.

questions.q: Who is the President of the International Chess Federation (FIDE)?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Arkady Dvorkovich as FIDE's President.

questions.explanation: The booklet describes Ju Wenjun as the reigning champion from China.

quizzes.title: Chess History and Indian Records
quizzes.passage:
Chess has a long history, and the World Chess Championship is one of the major titles in the game. The first official champion was the player who defeated Johannes Zukertort in the early contest for the title. Magnus Carlsen is a former World No. 1 in the sport.

Indian players have had strong results in recent years. Viswanathan Anand, India's most successful chess player, has won the FIDE World Chess Championship in several years, with titles spanning more than a decade. Koneru Humpy is India's highest-rated female chess player, and she has won the Women's World Rapid Chess Championship title.

Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 in Georgia, defeating Humpy Koneru in the final. She became the third winner of that title, after Alexandra Kosteniuk and Aleksandra Goryachkina.

In 2026, R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women's Candidates Tournament and became the first Indian woman to claim its title. She clinched the title by defeating Kateryna Lagno of Russia in the final round. Vaishali will challenge Ju Wenjun, the reigning champion from China, for the Women's World Chess Championship later in 2026.

Gukesh Dommaraju, India's youngest Grandmaster, became the youngest World Chess Champion after defeating Ding Liren of China.
